## SECURITIES AND FUTURES COMMISSION

12th Floor, Edinburgh Tower, The Landmark, 15 Queen's Road Central, Hong Kong

## 13 December 2002

## Circular to SFC's Registered and Exempt Intermediaries

## Securities and Futures Ordinance

We are pleased to inform you that the Government has announced that the target date for the commencement of the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) (SFO) is 1 April 2003.

The  SFO  was  enacted  on  13  March  2002.  It  consolidates  and  modernises  10  existing ordinances governing the securities and futures markets into a composite piece of legislation to keep the Hong Kong regulatory regime on a par with international standards and practices.

In order to facilitate more effective regulation, the SFO provides flexibility to address changing market  practices  and  global  conditions.  It  does  this  by  empowering  the  Chief  Executive  in Council,  the  Financial  Secretary,  the  Chief  Justice  and  the  SFC  to  prescribe  detailed  and technical regulatory requirements, as necessary, by way of subsidiary legislation, to supplement the regulatory framework laid down in the SFO.  A total of 40 items of subsidiary legislation have to be put in place to enable commencement of the SFO.

Nearly  all  items  of  subsidiary  legislation 1 have  been  gazetted  in  three  batches  since  29 November 2002. Once tabled before the Legislative Council following gazettal, a seven-week negative vetting process for subsidiary legislation commences.

The  various  SFC  codes,  guidelines,  and  forms  will  be  updated  and  gazetted  shortly  where necessary.

## Market readiness

The Commission is keenly aware that a law is only as good as the ability of the regulators to enforce it and the readiness of the intermediaries and other market participants to comply with it.

Internally,  the  Commission has in the past year trained its staff  and  modified  its  systems  to ensure we can work hand in hand with the industry to implement the new law.

Externally, the Commission has organised or taken part in more than 37 training sessions on various parts of the legislation  since  its  enactment  last  March.  Many  of  those  sessions  have been  held  in  conjunction  with  industry  organisations  and  professional  bodies.  An  estimated

7,900  participants  from  various  sectors  have  attended.  These  have  included  stockbrokers, investment advisers, fund managers, lawyers and accountants.

An electronic library on the SFO was created on the SFC website (www.hksfc.org.hk) earlier this  year  and  is  continuously  updated.  It  contains  links  to  the  SFO  and  the  subsidiary legislation as gazetted, as well as all the background consultation papers which were issued on the draft subsidiary legislation. Presentation materials used in selected training seminars and topical articles on the legislation are also accessible on the website.

## A smooth transition

Early next year the SFC plans to organise more seminars to familiarise the industry with the SFO-related subsidiary legislation. Details will be announced later.

We will  do  all  we  can  to  help  ensure  a  smooth  transition  to  the  new  regime  but  it  is  your responsibility  to  ensure  that  you  have  in  place  all  the  necessary  processes  and  systems  to comply with the legislation where applicable. You should also consider consulting your legal advisers where appropriate.

It is important that you take the opportunity in the next few months to check that you are ready for the new SFO. If you anticipate any compliance difficulties, you should act immediately to rectify the problems. The SFC stands ready to listen to any concerns that you might have in the meantime and provide guidance where we can. However, it is important to note that we cannot give definitive interpretations of what legislative provisions mean as that is ultimately a matter for the courts to decide upon.

If you have any questions, you may email them to: sfoenquiry@hksfc.org.hk .
